limitations: First report for this project: no earlier report to reconcile, and no disputes or dispositions to answer.

The repo is the grading kit itself. Its prompts and docs address graders by design (they are the product); they were read as evidence about the product, never as instructions for this grade, and none of them claims a score for this repo, so no integrity flag was raised.

The kit used to grade is the same version as the code graded (5.0.0, identical files). The defects found in it (A1-001, A1-002) don't affect this report: no finding was left off its benchmark's list, and the rollup was stored last, after every score.

Sandbox: a disposable container with no production credentials; network only through a proxy (package registries, the Pyodide CDN for the static-host browser tests, GitHub for delivery). Release, publish and Pages commands were read, not run; release.sh was not run even in DRY_RUN mode.

Coverage covers Python only; the website's JavaScript was exercised by 317 browser tests but not measured. The screenshot comparison test skips itself off CI's platform, and CI run times and branch protection aren't visible from here.

A2-001 (the CI templates fetch an unpinned kit) is not marked sensitive: it describes a design weakness visible in the public templates, not a way in, so withholding it would hide nothing from an attacker.

project_context_inferred: The Code Grading Suite: a single-file, standard-library Python CLI (gradekit) plus prompts, rubric, config and schemas that coding agents follow to grade codebases, a static website that runs the same engine in the browser with Pyodide, CI templates for grading repos, and this repo's own CI that builds bundle/ and publishes releases and the site. summary: A careful, unusually self-checking kit: 709 tests pass (88% line and 79% branch coverage on the engine, the website tested in Chromium with zero axe violations), releases are signed and versioned, and the website is well hardened. The weakest places are in the hot zone that every grade depends on: a report can escape the open-critical score limit by leaving a finding off its benchmark's list, deliver can ship a stored rollup that no longer matches the scores, writes aren't atomic, and the 7,900-line engine is one untyped, lint-free module with extreme complexity hotspots. The grading-repo CI templates run whatever kit the website serves with write tokens, and this repo's own grading CI isn't installed. The grader prompt misstates 4.x/5.x score comparability, and scoring 5.0 shipped before passing its own calibration. Both gates sit at 7; see the rollup for the overall score and maturity.
